publicationStmt.p: Working authority file for the Digital Corpus of Armenian Colophons. Publication details and licensing will be established for the corpus.

sourceDesc.p: Manuscript records will be compiled from catalogues, manuscript images, reviewed colophon witnesses, and supporting scholarship. The evidence for each description will be recorded.

projectDesc.p: This file identifies the manuscript objects associated with the corpus. A manuscript can preserve several colophons; a colophon can survive in several manuscripts. Particular occurrences of a colophon, their loci, and their transmission status are recorded in witnesses.xml. Transcriptions, translations, and detailed image alignment remain in the colophon files.

editorialDecl.p: Manuscript identifiers use readable city, collection where needed, and shelfmark components, for example ms-Yerevan-288, ms-Paris-Arm-178, and ms-Venice-SanLazzaro-17. Allocate each identifier once and retain it if the shelfmark, repository, dating, or attribution changes. Record current shelfmarks in msIdentifier and former shelfmarks in altIdentifier.
Use one msDesc per identifiable manuscript, inside listBibl.

Record manuscript production dates and places in history/origin with evidence and uncertainty. Do not equate the date narrated by a copied colophon with the date of its surviving manuscript. Date attributes such as when, notBefore, and notAfter will be added only when supported and interpreted according to the project's calendar conventions.

Use msPart for codicologically distinct units when necessary, including reused flyleaves. Do not introduce msPart for every folio or colophon. Unit-specific contents, hands, dates, and provenance belong to the relevant part. A witness can reference that part's stable identifier. Descriptions of fragmentary or dispersed objects will be refined through actual cases.

Bibliographical references will point to listbibl.xml when its records are populated. Catalogue citations supplied for these examples are retained inline until then. Local image paths and verified catalogue or viewer links can be recorded as digital surrogates; individual colophon image regions will be linked in the edition. Each scholarly assertion should remain traceable to its source.
